notes.title: SPAAs incoming (FIRST LOOK)!
notes.notes:
Christmas is coming, and we want to show you the self-propelled anti-aircraft vehicles inbound to WWII Online! A quick video (within the article) will show you instantly that these weapon platforms are going to have a BIG impact on the game for Pilots and AA gunners. One thing is for sure, we can't wait to see you guys go nuts with these things in-game. This will mark the first truly new vehicle that CRS 2.0 has added to the game and internally we couldn't be more ecstatic about expanding our development capabilities. So buckle up, it's Friday update time!

[h1][b]SELF-PROPELLED ANTI-AIRCRAFT[/b][/h1]

[url=https://youtu.be/zgP3RMBK1EQ]WATCH THE SHORT VIDEO HERE[/url]

We couldn't be more thrilled to show these vehicles off! Here's a first look at the Sdkfz 7 (SPAA) with a Flak28 mounted on top and the Allied (shared) Crusader (SPAA) with a Bofors on top. These vehicles will be able to be multi crewed (or individually) and the possibilities of dynamic placement on the battlefield is going to be a very big deal. AA platforms will now be in new areas previously unseen because of its self-propelled ability and armor columns will likely have greater anti-air support.

We have also added a couple of spots for infantry to ride on these vehicles for extra protection and/or increased logistics capabilities. Ride with a SPAA and protect it from infantry / spot for it!

[quote]
[b]THIS IS A [u]GAME CHANGER[/u] FOR AA GUNNERS & PILOTS![/b]
[/quote]

[h1][b]DEVELOPMENT ROADMAP UPDATE INCOMING[/b][/h1]
Each new year we work to update and revise our development roadmap to make sure we keep you guys briefed on the most important information available with regards to our development plans. First, let me say that the previous year has been a huge success for us in terms of unlocking new found development capabilities that were long lost. Our new Cornered Rat Software team (and company) has been maturing quite a bit and our delivery capabilities have grown exponentially these last 12 months.

We have a saying with this team that we take very seriously, and that is: "Underpromise, over deliver." When we make a commitment to you, it is our full intention to accomplish that mission. Sometimes these things take longer than we expect (or desire), and we make improvements where possible. So our 2018 roadmap plan will include [b]delivery[/b] on several items we have mentioned relating to new content introduced to WWII Online that was unable to be released during 2017. Several of these action items are actually in progress, some are almost completed.

The High Explosive and Kinetic Energy audits absorbed far more time than any of us expected from a production delivery stand point and will be coming in the 1st Quarter of 2018. Our current priority is to make sure you guys have a great Christmas and we get you some new stuff and fixes (some un-announced).

[h1][b]1.36 QUESTIONS & ANSWERS[/b][/h1]
I've spent some important time answering as many player questions as I can right now about what to expect with our next major version (1.36) which covers the Hybrid Supply system (a combination of moveable brigades and town based supply). This is a pretty important topic which will change the game as you know it to be played from a strategic perspective and should definitely read up on it.

[url=http://forums.wwiionline.com/forums/topic/415373-136-vital-questions/]Check out the 1.36 vital questions and answers located (here).[/url]

[h1][b]CRS IS WORKING HARD FOR YOU![/b][/h1]
We've been so busy grinding in the day-day that our communication has been a little less as of late. Sorry about that, there's so much to do that we've been slammed. Just wanted to make a quick comment here that everything is solid and we're ecstatic about our progress being made. I can't wait to get you that development roadmap coming and share with you our vision of what 2018 is going to look like.

Stay patient and optimistic guys, we're poised to have a substantial year ahead of us and with your continued support, that is going to be possible for us to continue on this forward track of progression! - WOOOOOOT!

notes.title: Game Play, HC, Production and CRS Planning
notes.notes:
CRS is back to the planning table with making big changes to the state of Campaign game play, and the High Command system. In addition we are opening up some new doors relating to content development (production), and some planning for CRS and our future. We're going into some details today about all of these subjects.

 
[h1]GAME PLAY PLANNING[/h1]
As you know not long ago we were talking about 1.36, which was discussed as the removal of the brigade system. Now that we've had sometime to muster more ideas and think on this subject, we're back to the planning boards considering exactly how we're going to approach this very important, game changing subject.

What we do know is, what we currently have is not working. The drain on High Command is substantial, the non-HC players do not really have control over where they want to attack, and the game's operation is at the mercy of volunteers actually being online and being knowledgeable to know how to respond to a variety of significant challenges. The consequences of not having those volunteers online negatively impact the entire state of the game both in the literal sense of major breakouts and cut offs, as well as the under the surface core of every individual: morale.

What we are discussing at this stage includes keeping a form of garrison supply at every town, both on the frontline and one town adjacent from the frontline as we had originally planned for, but instead of completely removing flags, we are now discussing leaving some flag movement capabilities in, with the intention of offering dynamically created game play (content) spear-headed by players, should they choose to.

The unique difference in what we originally proposed (which we still confidently believe will work to sustain the campaign which is why we want to keep it) versus this option, is to make sure that the map does not become something that people know exactly how to capture. In the past (with town based supply only), you could see High Command and players attacking a sequential pattern of towns, knowing that their demise would come with certainty due to the strategic value of neighboring towns. While this still exists to some degree, the flag system does help prevent the monotony that could come from this.

Therefore having moveable flags be an optional "spice-things-up," and not a game breaker (because these flags would not be nearly as stacked / powerful as they are according to today's standards) there's inherent value in doing this. In addition, it caters to a portion of our customer base that is concerned with the complete withdrawal of some moveable supply. We feel strongly that the player base as a whole will get behind this.

[h1]HIGH COMMAND WILL BE HERE TO STAY[/h1]
Our mission of High Command remains the same, we want them to play an important part in the betterment of the community and the Campaign. The future of HC will have a bit less control on the player base because supply will be more readily available across the frontline, and we're also considering ways for organic leadership and followers to initiate Attack Objectives merely by their presence (via proximity from a town). 

Shortly after these important game play changes go into effect, we'll then look to rebuild the HC system so it is a ground up organization, not a top down one. This means we'll be associating Squads once again with HC units and take a stroll back in time to learn from our lessons about what worked versus what has not. Today's HC system promotes too rapid growth of HC officers that are underdeveloped (mostly) and do not recall what it means to work your way up the chain of command and learn the new positions as you go along, eventually making you highly prepared.

Because of the demand HC has on their shoulders, including the consequences of their mistakes resulting into community backlash, HC is really considered more of a job than it is a force for the creation of fun (which was the original intent of creating HC). Facilitating in-game operations and out of game organization is really essential. If said leaders are promoted upwards from the bottom, people will follow those leaders more, and so the cycle of developing genuine leaders can be achieved.

CRS wants High Command to stay and we are committed to that happening. During our analysis of what the HC was supposed to be, what it became and now since the current brigade system has come, we found we had better outcomes and community engagement / player happiness / hc happiness in previous circumstances. While we do not consider today's HC a failure, it is undoubtedly not sustainable on this current trajectory, and it would be very unfair for us to not be upfront and identify the needed changes to remove these burdens from HC and the community they serve.

[h1]PRODUCTION IS OPENING NEW DOORS[/h1]
With our recent call for volunteers we've had a few new folks come onboard, and if you are interested in helping CRS do more, please consider a volunteer role and go to http://www.wwiionline.com/volunteer.

We are happy to report that we are now training two new artists on how to use the Creator program to give SADGUY a bit of relief and extra help. Scotsman has also been helping expedite development of new content while our guys are routinely following a production plan we have set to bring you new content.

We are also happy to report to you that while it will be a long road ahead of us, we now have a dedicated volunteer learning how to use our Terrain Editor system and we're trying to educate him with all that we have. We know there are some terrain fixes required and we are eager to bring forth improved terrain and perhaps some new play area changes to help spice the battlefield up. We'll keep you posted on progress here but it's going to be a little slow because the software is dated and clunky (hooray!). Regardless, the fact that CRS is now approaching this subject is very important to show our commitment in making sure we open up all available avenues to bring you fixes and new forms of content.

[h1]FUTURE PLANNING IS UNDERWAY FOR CRS[/h1]
We're planning consistent development of WWII Online in all forms possible and we're going to continue down this road of improving our game bringing you fixes and content where possible.

It is my personal mission that we always succeed as best as we can and that means looking at the future. I am starting to put together a plan of what our future will look like and our pathway to modernizing the game. As I've mentioned in the past, it is my intention to put together a second development wing at Cornered Rat Software that focuses on newer tech to help drive our forward progress. This is beginning very soon and we will be getting a group together to start developing newer gen assets and learn how to use the Unreal Engine (4).

Our primary wing (1) will be dedicated to WWII Online as we know it today. We understand it is vital for us to make sure we're giving you the best service possible. The goal in bringing this information forward is to make clear our intentions to ensure that we have a strong future ahead of us. To do so we must move seriously in the modernization of things in all ways possible.

In terms of a WWII Online 2.0, we're putting together a plan to achieve that. This will include a multiple phase battle plan to make this a reality. Since we are still a bit understaffed and have very tight resources it makes going all out on a significant project of that nature (scope and size) incredibly difficult. So our first mission is to outline the path of least resistance to achieve said resources and develop something within the realm of our resources and capabilities. With the clear understanding that there is no outside investment to come and we're going to have to do this together, community and CRS.

I will share more details of the plans as they are refined but the primary objective in mentioning this today is to plant the seed and be transparent, as that is what you deserve and we strive to provide. CRS will remain a hardcore realistic company focusing on war games.

To be clear; WWII Online is our flagship product and dear to our heart, we are going to be continuing what we're doing. If we want to achieve a second version of it, we have a lot of work to do and must follow a very specific path to make it successful. 

Please feel free to leave comments here, or you can send me an e-mail directly at xoom@corneredrats.com and I'd be happy to talk with you about any of this further.

Thanks for reading, see you in the field. SALUTE!

Matt "Xoom" Callahan
President & CEO
Cornered Rat Software
XOOM@CorneredRats.com

The future of HC will have a bit less control on the player base because supply will be more readily available across the frontline, and we're also considering ways for organic leadership and followers to initiate Attack Objectives merely by their presence (via proximity from a town). 

Shortly after these important game play changes go into effect, we'll then look to rebuild the HC system so it is a ground up organization, not a top down one. This means we'll be associating Squads once again with HC units and take a stroll back in time to learn from our lessons about what worked versus what has not. Today's HC system promotes too rapid growth of HC officers that are underdeveloped (mostly) and do not recall what it means to work your way up the chain of command and learn the new positions as you go along, eventually making you highly prepared.

Because of the demand HC has on their shoulders, including the consequences of their mistakes resulting into community backlash, HC is really considered more of a job than it is a force for the creation of fun (which was the original intent of creating HC). Facilitating in-game operations and out of game organization is really essential. If said leaders are promoted upwards from the bottom, people will follow those leaders more, and so the cycle of developing genuine leaders can be achieved.

CRS wants High Command to stay and we are committed to that happening. During our analysis of what the HC was supposed to be, what it became and now since the current brigade system has come, we found we had better outcomes and community engagement / player happiness / hc happiness in previous circumstances. While we do not consider today's HC a failure, it is undoubtedly not sustainable on this current trajectory, and it would be very unfair for us to not be upfront and identify the needed changes to remove these burdens from HC and the community they serve.

[h1]PRODUCTION IS OPENING NEW DOORS[/h1]
With our recent call for volunteers we've had a few new folks come onboard, and if you are interested in helping CRS do more, please consider a volunteer role and go to http://www.wwiionline.com/volunteer.

We are happy to report that we are now training two new artists on how to use the Creator program to give SADGUY a bit of relief and extra help. Scotsman has also been helping expedite development of new content while our guys are routinely following a production plan we have set to bring you new content.

We are also happy to report to you that while it will be a long road ahead of us, we now have a dedicated volunteer learning how to use our Terrain Editor system and we're trying to educate him with all that we have. We know there are some terrain fixes required and we are eager to bring forth improved terrain and perhaps some new play area changes to help spice the battlefield up. We'll keep you posted on progress here but it's going to be a little slow because the software is dated and clunky (hooray!). Regardless, the fact that CRS is now approaching this subject is very important to show our commitment in making sure we open up all available avenues to bring you fixes and new forms of content.

[h1]FUTURE PLANNING IS UNDERWAY FOR CRS[/h1]
We're planning consistent development of WWII Online in all forms possible and we're going to continue down this road of improving our game bringing you fixes and content where possible.

It is my personal mission that we always succeed as best as we can and that means looking at the future. I am starting to put together a plan of what our future will look like and our pathway to modernizing the game. As I've mentioned in the past, it is my intention to put together a second development wing at Cornered Rat Software that focuses on newer tech to help drive our forward progress. This is beginning very soon and we will be getting a group together to start developing newer gen assets and learn how to use the Unreal Engine (4).

Our primary wing (1) will be dedicated to WWII Online as we know it today. We understand it is vital for us to make sure we're giving you the best service possible. The goal in bringing this information forward is to make clear our intentions to ensure that we have a strong future ahead of us. To do so we must move seriously in the modernization of things in all ways possible.

In terms of a WWII Online 2.0, we're putting together a plan to achieve that. This will include a multiple phase battle plan to make this a reality. Since we are still a bit understaffed and have very tight resources it makes going all out on a significant project of that nature (scope and size) incredibly difficult. So our first mission is to outline the path of least resistance to achieve said resources and develop something within the realm of our resources and capabilities. With the clear understanding that there is no outside investment to come and we're going to have to do this together, community and CRS.

I will share more details of the plans as they are refined but the primary objective in mentioning this today is to plant the seed and be transparent, as that is what you deserve and we strive to provide. CRS will remain a hardcore realistic company focusing on war games.

To be clear; WWII Online is our flagship product and dear to our heart, we are going to be continuing what we're doing. If we want to achieve a second version of it, we have a lot of work to do and must follow a very specific path to make it successful. 

Please feel free to leave comments here, or you can send me an e-mail directly at xoom@corneredrats.com and I'd be happy to talk with you about any of this further.

Thanks for reading, see you in the field. SALUTE!

Matt "Xoom" Callahan
President & CEO
Cornered Rat Software
XOOM@CorneredRats.com

notes.title: Incoming Fixes and Features
notes.notes:
Our Production team is very focused on content delivery, in the form of fixes and features. Today we'll be going over some specifics and then generalize a bit about our approach and process. Now that we have crested the big "Steam" goal there's much more for us to do that players have been asking for, we hope this helps inform you that we're listening and taking action to, "make it so." One quick note for our Steam users: The resolution issues some have you have had, is being worked on with great priority and we have a hopeful fix currently in testing - thanks for your feedback. Also don't forget, this Sunday is OPERATION PLUNDER at 12PM Server Time. Okay, on with the production team!
[h1] [/h1][h1][b]FIXING EXISTING CONTENT[/b][/h1]
First, making sure that we have bugs or bad data fixed as quickly as possible, with an emphasis on how they perform according to historical values with several resources supporting them. I am proud to say we have a sincerely [u]dedicated to reality[/u] team working on ensuring the most genuine experience possible.

Here are [b]some[/b] of the things coming in our plan...
[list][*]Morris tractor braking (slide) issue[/*][*]NEW: High Explosive mechanism[/*][*]REVAMPED: New (and accurate) data for Kinetic Energy (non-explosive) projectiles[/*][*]Small arms audit: Improving how all infantry weapons perform[/*][*]Armor audit: Reviewing all armor thickness, armor types, etc[/*][*]Secondary damage state on some city buildings need review / cleaning up, and are temporarily disabled[/*][*]Replacing legacy artwork[list][*]Crewmen[/*][*]Vehicles[/*][/list][/*][/list][h1][b]INTRODUCING NEW CONTENT[/b][/h1]
Second we want to make sure that we're introducing new content. This is a vital component to improve quality of game play and community / subscriber health.

Here are [b]some[/b] of the things coming in our plan...
[list][*]Tank Busters[list][*]Junkers 87-G2[/*][*]Hurricane Mk II D[/*][*]P39-D Airacobra[/*][/list][/*][*]Self-proppeled anti aircraft vehicles[list][*]Sdkfz 7/2 with Flak28[/*][*]Crusader with Bofors[/*][/list][/*][*]New infantry characters[list][*]US Airborne Paratrooper[list][*]All paratroopers will receive similar load outs as other paratroopers in-game[/*][/list][/*][*]Italian soldier[list][*]Embedded with the German army persona[/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*]New infantry weapons'[list][*]STG44 (German)[/*][*]M1A1 Carbine (Allied)[/*][*].30 Caliber LMG (Allied)[/*][*]Carcano Rifle (Italy)[/*][*]Beretta SMG (Italy)[/*][/list][/*][/list][h1][b]MORE BATTLE PLANNING UNDERWAY[/b][/h1]
We're also collaborating to see what ways we can introduce new equipment and features to the game more rapidly. This list that you see above is our current and initial focus and by no means is it a simple list. 

Great things are happening here at Cornered Rat Software, our Steam release is purely amplifying that success further.

[h1][b]STEAM RESOLUTION FIX INBOUND[/b][/h1]
For our Steam users who have had a resolution issue, please note that we do have a fix on the way that is currently in testing. We're continuing to keep a close eye on things there to make sure you're being heard and having every reason to get into the game quickly.

[h1][b]SUBSCRIBING = FASTER DEVELOPMENT (SERIOUSLY!)[/b][/h1]
And finally it goes without saying that by subscribing to the game you will help us accomplish a lot more development work. Please consider doing that to help me bring more hands on more full time, that would be a huge boost to everything we're doing.

http://steamcommunity.com/games/251950/announcements/detail/1468595535778976538

That's all for this week, plenty of good stuff happening!

notes.title: Campaign 142 starts Sunday!
notes.notes:
This Sunday between 10-11AM Server Time (Texas - US Central) we will be starting Campaign 142. Until then, ALL WEAPONS & VEHICLES are available for play during our intermission phase (Friday & Saturday). 

The start of a Campaign is very important and quite busy. We'll be starting out in Tier 0 which means we'll have 1939-40 equipment. US Forces do not come in until Tier 3 so it will be the Germans versus the British and French. [i]Tiers are the progression of years in WWII Online. Each Tier (year) introduces new equipment.[/i]

The Campaign is a sacred thing here at WWII Online, it is the ultimate competition where both sides clash for total victory. Show up with a renewed sense of dedication and work hard to communicate. Apply all that you have learned during Campaign 141 and start fresh / ready to kill.

[h1]SUBSCRIBE TO & SUPPORT WWII ONLINE[/h1]

For some of you the 30 day trial we gave you of the premium subscription will be ending soon (as it's almost been 30 days since signing up). We hope that you have enjoyed your time and come to love our game and community.

Your subscription (DLC on Steam) goes to support our efforts by keeping our game servers, hosting and staff members paid for. To those of you already subscribing, thank you for your support and we hope many more join the effort to helping us take this game even further. Be sure to let other community members know the value in subscribing and helping them along, you may be surprised at how many folks do not know that we're some of the little guys trying to take this game to the next level / to the modern era.

Have a [url=http://www.wwiionline.com/roadmap]look at our roadmap[/url] for more details about what we're trying to do.

https://youtu.be/s_05bTbLvT8

[h1]PREMIUM SUBSCRIPTION[/h1]

[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/667291/World_War_II_Online__PREMIUM/]Premium Subscription = Full Access. Earn rank and unlock all weapons / join High Command.[/url]

[h1]STARTER SUBSCRIPTION[/h1]

[url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/667290/World_War_II_Online__STARTER/]Starter Subscription = Medium Access. Earn rank and unlock several weapons.[/url]

[h1]STEAM PLAYER FEEDBACK & DEVELOPMENT[/h1]

We're listening carefully to the feedback we're receiving and working on solutions to problems customers are encountering. We decided to launch in Early Access very intentionally so we had time before our primary release to fix things that were specific to this steam community.

We ask for you to give us the opportunity to absorb feedback and turn results. Give us a chance in the forums to interact with you and know that we take your feedback seriously.

[h1]WE'RE GROWING THE FANBASE![/h1]

We are very happy to report that our fanbase is indeed growing and our new generation of players coming from Steam are really enjoying our game. 

We have found those who are most successful in our game do the following:
[list][*]Join Discord (www.wwiionline.com/discord)
[*]Join a veteran squad
[*]Ask questions, Discord or F6 (Help) channel
[*]Give the game a bit of time[/list]

You are encouraged to follow those steps for the best experience possible.

Well that's all for now guys, keep telling your friends, keep letting us know how we can make things better (with every gripe, provide a solution - otherwise we can't fix it!), and most importantly, continue having an awesome time!

Cornered Rat Software

notes.title: Updating legacy art and weapon performance data
notes.notes:
Well we're now 100% released on Steam and the team has done a pretty solid job at improving stability of the Campaign server. We're keeping a watchful eye on the feedback coming from new Steam users and how we can improve their onboarding experience to WWII Online. Today we're going to cover a bit of Production and things happening in the pipeline now that we've crested this major milestone of getting the game onto Steam. This includes us improving some legacy art, and today we'll unveil the new iconic 88mm model that is inbound to the game shortly.

[h1]NEW 88MM MODEL INBOUND[/h1]

One of the oldest models we have in game at this stage is a real eye sore. A major thanks to SADGUY for focusing his energy on getting this iconic weapon to look tremendously better and brought into the modern era.

[img]http://www.wwiionline.com/images/production/new88-1.jpg[/img]

This will dramatically impact how bombs explode, including the type of fragmentation they throw and the affects it has on opposing vehicles. notes.title: Released to the World!
notes.notes:
WWII Online is now available to the WORLDWIDE! Download the main game and grab the premium DLC to support our team and game! Everyone can join the game now so spread the world, let the full WAR in Europe begin! ALL SOLDIERS REPORT TO BATTLE - AND BRING  A FRIEND!

[h1]Here's some important information for you:[/h1]
[list][*]A couple of known issues and fixes are here: http://steamcommunity.com/app/251950/discussions/0/1473095965308565026/
[*]Join our discord at http://wwiionline.com/discord
[*]Join our discussions area for help here: http://steamcommunity.com/app/251950/discussions/
[*]Our guides can be found here: http://steamcommunity.com/app/251950/guides/[/list]

[h1]TUTORIALS REDUCED & IMPROVED[/h1]

We have reduced and improved basic training from 5 tutorials down to 3 (Shoot, Move, Communicate). We've been listening to our Steam player feedback and made rapid adjustments - thanks all!

[h1]HOW TO SUCCEED IN OUR GAME[/h1]
[olist][*]Complete your mandatory 3 tutorials.
[*]Get on Discord asap (link above).
[*]Join a squad and participate with them.
[*]Ask questions! Use F6 for our help channel if you get stuck.
[*]Be patient. This game takes a little time to warm up to, it's not a turn key instant-gratification game.
[*]Give us a proper chance: Spend sometime in it and learn how awesome our game can be before giving up.
[*]Focus on surviving first, killing will come in time.[/olist]

Communication and allowing us to help you is the bottom line. This game has a steep learning curve, go into it knowing that. If you give it a proper chance (by being patient and learning) you will love the outcome.

[h1]SUPPORT / HELP[/h1]

If you get stuck or need help for any reason our support team is waiting for you:

http://support.wwiionline.com

[h1]TELL YOUR FRIENDS[/h1]

We would thoroughly appreciate you guys recruiting some new players to our game, we have to work together to build our population up. Form a squad and conquer Europe!

[h1]OUR THANKS TO YOU[/h1]

For your tremendous support and patience while releasing on Steam. We know many of you were chomping at the bit to get in and had to wait a bit. We would've rather avoided that but the time we spent making some changes was for the betterment of all the new folks coming on board.

Cornered Rat Software is so grateful to be here and to have your backing. We hope you fall in the love with the game as we have and help us take it to the next level.

SALUTE - AND GET IN GAME!

notes.title: Fixing remaining issues - hang in there!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, we are working as quickly as we can to make some improvements on the total amount of training newcomers are required to do and fix resolution issues being reported. We are taking in your feedback and translating that into actionable results to improve the on boarding experience for more users inbound to WWII Online.

Our schedule is being pushed because of those things a little bit and we apologize for the delay, but recognize as we have that the wait will be worth it so you do not experience some issues the Steam early-birds did.

Steam user feedback has been an important guide for us to make these improvements. We decided on a staggered roll out plan very intentionally and it is working precisely as we had planned.

We know many of your are chomping at the bit to get into the game and we love seeing that enthusiasm. Since we have released in Early Access (very strategically) this should give you a sign that some fixes were bound to happen. As we have promised all along we'd be listening closely to that feedback and making improvements immediately upon landing here.

Thank you so much for your patience. We will get you into the game as quickly as we can, but we want to make sure the issues that some of your fellow community members had, will not be your first experience with us.

We will keep you posted on our release date(s) as quickly as we can, we are working very hard this entire weekend to get you into the game with a goal by next week.

S! (Salute) from Cornered Rat HQ.

notes.title: Update on Release Schedule
notes.notes:
Good morning everyone.

I wanted to come give you an update on the rollout status for today. 

As you know, we had scheduled the release of the game for Europe today. [b] Unfortunately we've made the decision to postpone the full release to Europe in order to address some of the resolution issues that we've seen since the start of our Steam availability. [/b]

One of the biggest things that customers have been reporting and one of the things that has been the most has been the most frustrating to them is an inability to save changes to the game resolution.

Our development team has identified the issue causing this and has been working on a solution. The suspected cause for this behavior is non-standard characters in the file path (such as accented characters, for example). 

In order to allow for us to fully test the patch to correct this issue, we have decided to hold of on releasing to the majority of Europe until later in the week. 

[b]We will be opening up access to the UK and Ireland,[/b] as we feel that the potential for this problem to manifest itself in those areas is relatively lower than in the rest of Europe. 

We know that you all have been patiently watiting for the game to be available to you, and we appologize for making you wait a little longer. 

One of the reasons why we have been staggering the release is to be able to address issues such as this. We hope that you understand the reasoning behind this delay and [b]we expect to be able to release in the rest of Europe later in the week. [/b] 

We will keep you all updated as to when we expect this to occur. We do still expect to be fully released by September 22 as we originally stated.

notes.title: Thousands are flooding in!
notes.notes:
Thousands of new players are joining WWII Online as we speak! The game population has reached the highest levels it has in many years and we owe that to our new soldiers inbound from Steam, and to our existing guys who helped us make it happen - WOOT! [b]HOP IN GAME, MAJOR BATTLES UNDERWAY![/b]

Currently there at 5 AO's per side available which uses the underpopulated sides balancing logic we recently introduced. That means there are 10 battles at play fighting over ownership of Europe.

We're seeing players working together to tow in new vehicles, transport their friends around, join tank columns, run 70 man paratrooper drops, running fair mile (boats) down the river, and so much more - WOW! It's really exciting!

Here's a quick look at the German training ground as of this writing:

[img]http://www.wwiionline.com/images/busytraining.jpg[/img]

Every soldier must first complete some basic training so that they can be an effective and knowledgeable soldier.

[h1]TRAINING SUBJECTS INCLUDE[/h1]
[list][*]Movement
[*]Using the Rifleman
[*]Communicating in game
[*]Understanding your heads up display
[*]Navigating the map to find the battles[/list]

Please let your friends know about our game! Report for duty now, there is a WAR going on!

Need any account or technical help? support.wwiionline.com

notes.title: Roll out on Steam has begun!
notes.notes:
S! Steam Friends!

[h1]WWII Online is now rolling out in the Steam Store![/h1]

It has been a long road to get to this point for us at CRS and all of us are very excited to have Steam users in the game!

We're already seeing some great teamwork in game! (Not to mention some pretty epic paratrooper missions!)

I just wanted to take a moment to help everyone's transition onto the virtual battlefield! 

When you're joining the battle for the first time, you will launch the game and it will present you with several options including [b]Join the Battle[/b], [b]Training Server[/b], and [b]Play Offline[/b].

To get to the Main Campaign server, all you have to do is click the [b]Join the Battle[/b] button. 

This will launch you into the campaign. If it is the first time you've logged in, you will be required to complete the first 5 Training Tutorials. This will give you a basic understanding of some of the controls and how to use the map and the chat. 

Once you complete these, you'll be able to choose your side, select a squad, and join the battle!

[h1]A Couple of Issues We've Seen So Far[/h1]

Here are and a couple of quick links to some support articles regarding a couple of the common issues we've been seeing today:

[list]
[*]It's not allowing me to download: The store page is available to everyone, but the game is not yet available to all regions. Please take a look at the "News" Section here on Steam to see the release plan and when we expect the game to be available in your region. 

[*][url=www.wwiionline.com/dpi] DPI Scaling Issue: The game first loads, even with the correct resolution set, and it's too big for the screen. The player can only see a portion of the screen.[/url]

[*][url=www.wwiionline.com/personas-locked]All Personas Locked or Being Forced into Training: Some players are having an issue with seeing Red Locks on all personas or being forced into training even though they have passed all training.[/url]
[/list]

[quote=WWII Online Release Schedule]WWII Online will be released between September 5th - September 22nd 2017. This is to ensure best game experiences and ramp up our player numbers. These dates are subject to change based on outcomes of unlocking each region.

September 5th: Canada, Mexico and South America
September 8th: United States of America
September 12th: All of Europe
September 15th: All of Asia
September 19th: Oceania
September 22nd: The rest of the world[/quote]

notes.title: Friday Development Update - Free Play Improvements & Steam Launch
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! Hope you're getting excited! I wanted to share with you an update from XOOM about what's been happening here at RAT HQ. So without further ado... 

[quote=XOOM]Steam is launching shortly and everyone is excited! Today we have opened the doors to our "Welcome Back Soldiers," and we're also doing some last minute fixes on our game server in preparation for that big launch. Meanwhile we are here to announce some important Free Play subscription improvements that we think will improve the experience for new players joining our game beyond their initial trial period. I also have an update regarding our server infrastructure (cell hosts)... So buckle up, here we go![/quote]

 

[h1]RANK THRESHOLDS INCREASED (NOW LIVE)[/h1]

For a long time Free Play and Starter subscription users have been quickly hitting a wall in terms of progression. After some careful review the team at CRS has found a way to fix this, and allow Free Play and Starter subscribers to go from Rank 1 (Recruit) to Rank 13 (Lt. Colonel), while continuing to maintain the value and access behind each subscription type. 

This is a major development because progression for users is very critical. People want things to work towards and it will also incentivize these users to go to a Premium account at a later time once they earn more rank, likely increasing the probability to bigger levels than previous.

[h1]FREE PLAYERS CAN POST MISSIONS (LIVE)[/h1]

Missions are the gateway to accessing everything inside of the game, and since we want maximum flexibility for our users to rally up with their friends, this is another major development. It also means that these users won't get bottlenecked or cut off from the game at anytime. 

[h1]RESERVE SMG IS GOING TO STAY WITH FREE PLAY[/h1]

After very careful consideration we want our Free Play subscribers to be able to access the limited submachine gun. There was talk about them having a Rifle only, and while we agree that this is the most important soldier on the battlefield, we also wanted to actively work to give them a taste towards an automatic weapon. For our non-free play subscribers, consider retention of the users. We want people to keep coming back and playing the game, because a populated battlefield is the most important aspect of our massively multiplayer online game. That said, we may tweak the load out a little more and reserve the right to do so.

[h1]30 DAY TRIAL FOR STEAM USERS - DURING SEPTEMBER[/h1]

Because of our staggered roll out we are going to up the ante and create a maximum opportunity for our Steam users to get engaged and invested into WWII Online. Consider this an investment into these players. You will be able to keep all the rank you can earn and we've literally doubled the amount of free time you can get for everyone who signs up in September.

Possible option (decision to be made later): If this goes amazingly well, we may make the 30 day trial a default for Steam users. We're actually going to be testing quite a bit to see how this goes and we're happy with the decision for all of September. We want players in-game and having a good time to start a fantastic Steam launch, what better a way to welcome thousands of new community members?

So in a nut shell, these changes are all tailored to ensuring the best possible release and retention of users. We still feel confident that our other subscriptions maintain substantial value and hope users will learn to love our game and back up our small studio so we can expand our development capabilities, and more rapidly deploy new content and fixes.

[h1]CELL HOST(S) UPDATE[/h1]

Reminder: Cell Hosts manage the total amount of concurrent users we can have via load balancing.

So we've had to do quite a few server restarts this week, sorry about that. It is crunch time and we have to make quick changes to prepare for. The good news is our development team found a major memory leak issue between cell hosts and clamped it. So while your HITS might be showing up as 0, even if you have a Kill (1), don't worry about it we're still counting all of those.

There may be some more server restarts so brace yourself, and understand that this is super important to iron out a couple last issues. We really appreciate your patience on all of this. 

[quote][h1]STEAM RELEASE SCHEDULE[/h1]

WWII Online will be released between September 5th - September 22nd 2017. This is to ensure best game experiences and ramp up our player numbers. These dates are subject to change based on outcomes of unlocking each region.

[list][*]September 5th: Canada, Mexico and South America
[*]September 8th: United States of America
[*]September 12th: All of Europe
[*]September 15th: All of Asia
[*]September 19th: Oceania
[*]September 22nd: The rest of the world[/quote]

[h1]SPREAD THE WORD ABOUT STEAM LAUNCH![/h1]

On a final note, please make sure to mention on any relevant site or platform or network of friends that WWII Online is coming to Steam, and can be easily found if you navigate to www.wwiionline.com/steam. Your help in raising awareness will undoubtedly work towards improving the amount of traffic that shows up and will amplify our success.

Thanks for your support all, it's getting nuts around here!

notes.title: WWII Online Steam Release Date Announcement
notes.notes:
S! everyone, the time you have all been waiting for is close at hand!

Today we will be letting you all know our roll out plan for the Steam release of WWII Online!

Our plan is to begin rolling out the game by region starting on September 5! As we roll out, we will be monitoring all of our systems and ensuring that everything is running up to snuff and will continue to add users by region until we're available everywhere!

On September 5, we will be making the game available for all of North and South America (except the USA). 

We will then be releasing WWII Online to the USA on September 8, followed by Europe on September 12, Asia on September 15, and finally Oceania and the rest of the world on September 19. 

We're excited to get all of the Steam users into game! Due to the staggered nature of the release, we are going to be extending a special offer for all Steam users who sign up during the month of September we will be extending the 2 week trial to a full 30 days. 

Once this 30 day trial period is completed, users who do not subscribe to either the Starter or Premium subscription will be able to continue playing using the perpetual Free Play account. 

We would also like to announce some other special things we have planned to coincide with our release on Steam! 

First, we will be welcoming back all of our Veterans with a very special Welcome Back Soldier event! This Welcome Back Soldier will be different from any that we've done in the past, so if you're a veteran player, make sure to watch out for important communications from RAT HQ with the instructions on how to take part in this awesome promotion!

Second, the High Commands, in collaboration with the players and in game Squads, will be organizing several server wide operations that will bring your team together to face the enemy to capture strategic objectives all along the front line! Get in game and watch the forums for details on these great community events!

It's time to get your friends together and get ready to join the fight! An exciting new chapter in the history of WWII Online is about to begin!

The Virtual Battlefield does exist!

notes.title: Recommended: Microphone & Joystick
notes.notes:
Although they are not required to play, these two pieces of hardware will [b]fundamentally improve[/b] your game play experience. As a new player there's a lot to absorb so having voice comms (Discord) running with veteran soldiers will make you better understand all of the elements at play.

The game does offer text based communications and basic mouse + keyboard controllers, however you will have a serious competitive edge if you have these things first.

Our game runs Discord primarily for game communications, so even if you don't have a Microphone you can join up there and listen to everything else going on and be part of the fight in a much bigger way. [i]Seriously, get on voice comms,[/i] otherwise you'll miss out on a lot in terms of immersion and teamwork.

Air Combat most specifically is very hard to do with a mouse and keyboard, and since we're a bit simulation like you can imagine how that would go (possible, but not easy).

Your local electronics store(s) should have these items. This is just a courtesy heads up to give you a little time to prepare.

Steam release is not far away, we are testing the Steam release candidate organically (our current customer base / Non-Steam) right now to iron out any last minute kinks prior to launch day.

HANG IN THERE FOLKS! We know you're restless, we're trying to make your first experience a lot better.

Salute!

- Cornered Rat Software

notes.title: Subscriptions & Free Play - Explained
notes.notes:
Today I wanted to explain why our game is subscription based, and go into more details about our continuous Free Play subscription that we're offering. We think there's been some misconceptions about the typical "Free-To-Play" genre and how that relates to us, because while there are some correlations, there are also some pretty big differences.

Prepare for a bit of an informative wall of text (sorry in advance)!

[quote][h1]Free Play Subscription Improvements (NEW!)[/h1]

Addition to this article as of September 1st, 2017:

http://steamcommunity.com/games/251950/announcements/detail/1452829766970988580[/quote]

Let's get started with the Free Play subscription that we're offering.

[h1] Free Play - Continuous Subscription (Base Game)[/h1]

Anyone who signs up with WWII Online will receive [b]two full weeks of premium access[/b] which will allow you to earn as much rank as you can. You will have absolutely no commitment to put any money down during this time, and be able to try out all equipment that you have rank to access.

On day 15, if you have not selected a recurring subscription plan you will then receive the following equipment and game access [b]for as long as you choose.[/b]
[list]
[*] Rifleman
[*] Submachine Gunner (Limited Ammo)
[*] Truck
[*] Hauler (heavy truck)[/list]
[b]Rifleman Class:[/b] This is the backbone of any military and our game is no exception. Since you are fighting in a global war known as the, "Campaign," the capture of territory is very essential. As a Rifleman, you will have the following:
[list]
[*]Bolt-Action Rifle
[*]Fragmentation grenades
[*]Smoke grenades
[*]Knife
[*]Ammo can (resupply friendly troops primary ammo)
[*]Binoculars
[*]CP Captures[/list]
[b]Truck / Hauler Class:[/b] Moving troops and equipment on the battlefield in a war simulation is essential. You will play an important role in logistical operations and be capable of re-supplying any ground based vehicle. You can tow heavy and light anti-tank or anti-aircraft guns and move your friends around the battlefield.

You will have full chat functionality, be eligible to join missions and group up as squads, rank up to a Private First Class and be an active contributing member on our official game forums.

[b]Continuous Free Play, means continuous and unchanging.[/b] If you want to be a member of our community long-term, this is a zero risk or money down way to do it and still have a very big impact on the game.

[h1]Why is WWII Online subscription based?[/h1]

It's a fair question to ask in this day and age, but this has worked for [b]us[/b] very well over the years, and is core to the design of our game overall. We have been actively running this game since June 6th 2001, and our leap to Steam is a big one for us. We're also not under any illusions about the general skepticism about how we will perform.

But, we think we're offering a very fair product, meaning by not having micro-transactions we think we're actually doing a greater service in the name of fair game play than some of our competitors. Every rifleman in the game will have the exact same equipment and performance properties.

A micro-transaction game is not truly [b]Free-To-Play,[/b] and it certainly isn't balanced as it favors he who has the biggest wallet. This is an arguable point about WWII Online requiring some money down for a subscription (something we have been very upfront about this whole time), but our point in saying that is our price point is achievable and all-inclusive... you will not be nickeled and dime'd just to play.

You won't see any special ammo buys or other unrealistic monetization practices intended to incentivize you as a new player to pay up. 

We're genuinely interested in sharing our game with you and getting you to enjoy it, so we've carved out this Free Play subscription to remove any reason for someone to at least not try our game.

[quote]Our price point is achievable and all-inclusive... you will not be nickeled and dime'd just to play.[/quote]

[h1]I am interested in progression, how does this work?[/h1]

All of our subscriptions allow for you to progress your character in each persona (a persona is your character by country and service branch). To unlock more equipment and rank access to progress further, you will need to choose the Starter or Premium subscriber after your first two weeks.

[h1]What subscriptions do you offer?[/h1]
[list]
[*]Free Play (continuous): Base game, includes first 2 weeks of premium.
[*]Starter $7.99/mo: Includes additional weapons, vehicles, rank and access.
[*]Premium $14.99/mo: Includes all weapons, vehicles, rank and access.[/list]
[i]Access to vehicles and other weapons is rank dependent. Our subscriptions are handled as Downloadable Content (DLCs) on Steam.[/i]

[h1]What does this subscription go towards?[/h1]
[olist]
[*]Infrastructure: An MMO requires many servers, server housing / security, bandwidth (ISP), and on-site maintenance.
[*]Staffing: You're supporting a small indie development studio (developers, administrators, artists, producers, community and marketing managers, etc).
[*]Expansion: You will help us gain additional resources to further develop the game by adding more content and improvements.[/olist]

[h1]What if I don't want to subscribe?[/h1]

There is no obligation for you to subscribe. You will continue to have a Free Play account with the equipment we have listed above. [i]Our only request[/i] is that you continue to play the game and let your friends know about it!

[h1]What prompted this article?[/h1]

Cornered Rat Software wants to be [b]abundantly transparent[/b] about what we're offering and not mislead anyone. We value transparency and community interaction deeply and this subject is coming up in our Community Hub a bit as of late.

We want all of you to join our game and love it like we do, and once you're in and experience how awesome it can be, we really believe you will.

[h1]What prompted this article?[/h1]

Cornered Rat Software wants to be [b]abundantly transparent[/b] about what we're offering and not mislead anyone. We value transparency and community interaction deeply and this subject is coming up in our Community Hub a bit as of late.

We want all of you to join our game and love it like we do, and once you're in and experience how awesome it can be, we really believe you will.

notes.title: New HE Model, New UI and Population climbing!
notes.notes:
In our continued pursuit to provide the highest level of realism, Scotsman will be sharing the new High Explosive model with a screen shot and documentation that helps outline the major impact this will have on the game. We'll also show you a first look at the new "Steam" user integrated account creation and server selection screen, and outline our new "Basic Training Required" UI flow. Finally, we're encouraging Squads again this week to prepare to bring on new users, as we're already seeing a noticeable increase in population. Buckle up, the development train is moving full steam ahead!

[h1][b]NEW HIGH EXPLOSIVE MODEL[/b][/h1]

Cornered Rat Software has prioritized increasing the realism of our game and with the amazing efforts from Scotsman we are getting more realistic and efficient. We've talked a bit about the New HE model but today, we wanted to show case what this looks like to add some more context of how powerful this advancement is for all of our realism fanatics here at WWII Online! - Great job Scotsman!

[quote=From Scotsman (WWII Online Military Advisor)] The image you see below is of new HE data operating in the new HE model. The new data set correctly simulates every munition in the game for proper fragment size, mass, and velocity. Higher mass or higher velocity fragments reach further than smaller, lighter, or lower velocity fragments. There is variance in each and every explosion, no two explosions are alike, so you may be wounded in one instance and killed in another depending on the size and velocity of the fragments that hit you. All these distributions are built around the physical properties of the ammunition to include type of explosive fill, the amount of explosive, and the construction of the ammunition. Original factory production diagrams of all munitions were used to generate the data. Shell or bomb casing length, width, and wall thickness etc are all accounted for in the calculations.

Data generation is complete and this is going into Q&A testing. Expect it to go live shortly after steam along with many other changes. Updates in work include changes to the HEAT modeling, armor modeling, and a complete audit of small arms accuracy for all weapons. (prompted by forum user requests) This updates small arms performance to the like new factory acceptance standard firing standard WWII government issued ammunition.

You might also add that this means that bombs, mortars and HE will finally work as they should - same calculations as used in US Govt. weapons effects testing.[/quote]

[img]https://www.wwiionline.com/images/newhemodel.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]NEW STEAM USER LAUNCH SCREEN[/b][/h1]

As part of our plan to help simplify things for Steam users, we've taken into consideration the whole UI (user interface) flow for creating your account, and selecting your server. Below is our first iteration of how this will work, users will select "Join the Battle" which will be the Campaign server, of course there's the Training Server and Offline mode. Normally these things have been controlled outside of game but we figured it's time to start integrating it in, and we're quite pleased with how simple this has made things.

After Steam's release we'll begin examining how to do something similar for our organic (existing) user base as well.

[img]https://www.wwiionline.com/images/steamlaunchscreen.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]TRAINING REQUIRED - PERSONA SELECTION SCREEN[/b][/h1]

Here's a look at what new users will be presented with after they create their account and attempt to join either the Campaign or Training Server. Immediately new users will go into Basic Training so they can learn the basics of:
[olist] 
[*]Movement
[*]Rifleman usage
[*]How to chat with other players
[*]How to navigate the map and icons
[*]HUD "Heads Up Display" overview[/olist]
Once a player has completed these [b]mandatory[/b] training requirements, they will then select their persona of choice, and be prompted to join a WWII Online Squad. Training will become mandatory for both organic and Steam users (all) in an effort to better prepare users for the steep learning curve ahead. CRS believes that these basic things are an absolute necessity to give them the proper tools to be successful.

[img]https://www.wwiionline.com/images/trainingrequired.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]JOINING A SQUAD PROMPT - NEW USERS ORGANICALLY & STEAM[/b][/h1]

Immediately after a new player has completed their basic training requirements, they will be able to select a persona. They will be prompted with an active list of Squad recruiters who are online and in a mission at that time. We highly encourage all new users coming through the door to join up with a Squad as it will greatly improve your game experience here. This is entirely a team based game, and while we do offer lonewolf's to do their thing, organized numbers [b]will always win.[/b] 

By joining a Squad you will immediately get help with all of your questions and learn how to play the game. One of the biggest draw's of WWII Online is its scale and when your Squad is working together, on voice comms and heading towards a target, it's quite exhilarating and you can dominate otherwise unorganized forces.

[i]We shared this screen shot last week but wanted to display it again to have context to what we're saying above. [/i]

[img]https://www.wwiionline.com/images/Squad-Recruitment-Interface.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]NOTICEABLE POPULATION UP-TICK IN GAME[/b][/h1]

We have seen that we're seeing returning and new users join back up with the game in preparation for the upcoming Steam release. Folks are looking to build rank and gain a competitive edge and the Rats are more than welcoming it! We're also receiving confirmation that through this climb in numbers just how important the game population alone can dramatically improve battles in World War II Online. We have seen some AMAZING fights over the last couple of week's and I have personally been in-game with fellow Rats along side Squads on both the Allied and Axis side, it's been seriously awesome and is an encouraging factor of what's to come.

That's all for now this week, much more activity behind the scenes in progress.

- Cornered Rat Software

notes.title: Update from RAT HQ
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, time again for another update!

[b]Steam Release Candidate in Testing[/b]

So... some big news on the Steam front! This week, our Development team has been hard at work building release clients for testing! Even as I'm typing this, we have a big group of our team testing the latest alpha build!

Our testing has been going well and we're progressing to have a full release client in the near future! This is exciting since this is the major hurdle we have keeping us from releasing the game on Steam!

[b]Squads & Recruiting[/b]

One of the other things we've been working on this week is a way for new users joining the game to be able to choose a squad that is recruiting and be automatically placed in that squad and put in contact with the recriting player! We think this will be a great opportunity for both new players and squads to come together and take the fight to the enemy! This is a feature that is going to be evolving as we get feedback on how it's working, but we think that participation in squad game play can really enhance your experience in game, so we want to encourage folks to find one that fits their play style!

[b]Some clarification on the Free Play Account/Subscription[/b]

We've been seeing a lot of discussion here on the Steam forums, as well as on our own game forums about the Free Play Account offering that we'll be bringing to Steam and I want to talk about this for a minute. We'll start with a quote from XOOM in his latest development update:

[quote="XOOM"]World War II Online is and always has been a subscription based game. Our new players coming through Steam need to know that there's a fundamental difference in what we're offering as compared to today's typical "Free to Play (F2P)" type model. 

To get right to it, we [b]do not [/b]offer micro-transactions; in-game currency system, and you won't be nickel or dime'd to death just to select your weapon and play.

What [b]we do[/b] offer is fair game play with no item buys that gives you an advantage over another player; massive game play battle zones with hundreds of players interacting on the land / air / sea together in a single battle, advanced historically accurate damage modeling, a mature and helpful community, a pathway to try the game absolutely risk / money free and a whole lot more.

For your first two weeks you can play the game like a premium subscriber and be introduced to the entire game in the best possible way, for no commitment or money down. And if you decide you never want to subscribe, there's an option for you to play an integral part in the capturing of territory, and movement of supplies or equipment. You will still be able to join squads and participate in missions, communicate on the forums and in-game chat, we'll track your statistics and you'll continue to be able to play the game endlessly with the equipment set we've provided.

WWII Online is a massively multiplayer online game, with a lot of supporting infrastructure / services, and our staff is from all across the world that we have to take care of. As we are the definition of an indie studio we've made very careful considerations about how we're deploying on Steam, and we're consistently evaluating feedback to make sure we're still on par.

We hope that you'll enlist and see why WWII Online has been around for over 16 years, and hopefully fall in love with the game as we have.

We welcome questions or feedback, please be as constructive as you can and we'll take all matters into consideration.[/quote]

Hopefully this helps clarify what the Free Play account will allow if you should choose to not subscribe to a different subscription package. 

That's about it for now. We're getting excited as we're getting closer to launching on Steam!

Until next time...

notes.title: Friday Development Update from Xoom!
notes.notes:
Today's Development Update comes from XOOM!

Today we'll talk about the things we're doing to make our game more realistic; our equipment balancing strategy, and Steam's deployment status. Within Steam we'll cover how subscriptions for those users will be handled, cell hosts (what they are and why they're important), training tutorials now being a requirement and other preparations underway as launch day approaches. 
 
[h1]REALISM IS OUR PRIORITY[/h1]
We've been having some awfully long internal discussions about the current state of the game and the things that we are working on. Particularly with the inclusion of some upcoming content that we have on the shelf and getting their deployment plan all sorted out. One of the major topics that has come up as a very important reminder for us, is the requirement to have our game be as realistic as possible.

You can see our Production team already employing a higher sense of realism through their High-Explosive audit which is not far away from being employed into the game (first content release after Steam). Next up on the list is all other projectiles (kinetic energy, non-explosive). And following that will be a complete review of all armor plating types and their thickness. As a reminder, we can model armor thickness down to the millimeter (and to even greater fractions, but that's a bit overkill ~ still cool though).

[h1]EQUIPMENT BALANCING STRATEGY[/h1]
A discussion to reaffirm our position as being as realistic as possible and finding ways to balance our content standing by was very important to have. In the real war, there was not a 1 to 1 match for equipment. Two weapons standing out spurring that discussion currently includes the M1A1 Carbine and the STG44. There is a well known fact that the STG44 is a pretty amazing weapon, but we also know it was available later in the war with limited numbers, where as the M1A1 was pretty well mass produced. So how do we balance that? 

Well we can't very well hand off the STG44 to the Allied forces, or the M1A1 to the German forces. But we can reflect the total supply availability for equipment in their spawn lists as a means to provide a balance.

We think it's really important to employ this strategy as we move forward so our content pipeline doesn't get bottlenecked and we get stuck into a position with equipment sitting on the shelf for awhile, as in the case of these two weapons.

Fortunately, you will be seeing these two weapons in the near future. All content is being prepared for post-Steam deployment, as a means to maintain focus on the deployment of Steam itself, as well as provide some new content to maintain the interest and continued growth of those users, as well as our organic customer base.

[h1]STEAM DEPLOYMENT STATUS[/h1]

[b]SUBSCRIPTIONS ARE DLC'S ON STEAM[/b]

Things are looking very good here at the moment. Our Starter and Premium subscriptions are being setup as DLC's per how Steam's platform actually works, but they will be pretty visible for folks to see. Every Steam user will start out as a FREE PLAYER with a 2 week trial followed by a perpetually free (but limited) account (Rifleman, Trucks and Haulers only). As always they'll be able to subscribe right away at any time.

[b]CELL HOSTS - HOW MANY USERS CAN BE ONLINE[/b]

We have successfully tested two cell hosts (which manage players in the campaign) and per cell host we have been able to push 1200 bots on them, so effectively at this moment we can run 2400 concurrent players. As we have been saying we are expanding that limitation and theoretically with multi-cell repaired (the process that allows multiple cell hosts to be used) should work by default for cell host 3 & 4. The development and operations team are working closely on this particular item right now. Our mission is to deploy 4 cell hosts by Steam's release to hold the maximum number of users as possible.

[b]TRAINING TUTORIALS - NOW REQUIRED[/b]

Training Tutorials will not be able to be bypassed anymore for our new incoming users. This is an incredibly important period of time for the new users to be successful. With the complexity of WWII Online, if a user does not go through the basic tutorials they will have a much lesser percentage of knowing what to do or how to interact with other users / get into the game world.

Users will launch the game, and before proceeding beyond the persona selection screen they will be prompted to take a non-optional (mandatory) training session of the first 5 basic training tutorials, which include:

[list][*]Movement
[*]Rifle / weapons usage
[*]Chat
[*]Map / using map tools
[*]HUD (Heads up Display)[/list]

Once these tutorials are completed, which will take up to 15 minutes roughly depending on the speed of the user, they will be entered into the regular Campaign and officially start their career in WWII Online. Our team has invested some important time into making sure the tutorials were functioning and there were no road blocks that would cause an issue with users being stuck / unable to proceed. 

We think this is such an important development to ensure the highest levels of success not just for the user but for the game. This will get users into battle faster with more understanding, it is something that really should never be bypassed.

[b]GAME MANAGEMENT PREPARATIONS[/b]

Our new Game Manager "OHM" is preparing for the influx of users and is deep in understanding his new toolset and responsibilities. There will need to be an increase in supply and he'll be at the ready to carefully push numbers upwards as needed. He's also trying to get a new maintenance cycle established, with the hope of making it a bit less frequent and intrusive on Campaign operations. One thing is for sure: the Campaign server must continued to be reset, at a minimum of once per week. With the Campaign coming to new hardware shortly, there may be some changes that are unforeseen, so we'll keep you guys posted as this develops.

OHM is also considering how we can improve the landscape of intermissions and making them a bit more vibrant and interesting. If special events are something you are interested in, you should really connect with him, you can do so by sending him a forum PM.

COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT PREPARATIONS

KMS has been getting his mind blown with all of the stuff required for the Community Manager to do but he's a quick learner and embracing the responsibility. He's also processing a new Assistant Community Manager that will help him with the Axis High Command / Community, filling his recently held position. We'll be announcing who that is in the near future but we think he'll do a great job and the Axis community will be getting an awesome rep.

Keeping the community healthy is paramount for our CM team, so they are strategizing together about expectations and what to prepare for as Steam comes.

[b]HIGH COMMAND OFFICERS - ARE NEEDED (BIG TIME)[/b]

We're going to need an influx of High Command officers to support game operations around the clock for both AHC and GHC. If you can devote a minimum of 3 months service right before Steam's release the Rats would be very grateful. As you know we are deploying on Steam with the brigade system and need as many capable hands in there to help things out and make sure the game stays healthy. Please see the community management team or your HC office for greater details.

[h1]OVERALL PROGRESS - STRONG[/h1]

Thousands of new players are learning about our game everyday, and that's really exciting for us. Steam is continuing to show its power in terms of traffic as it is generating an impressive number of impressions, clicks, Steam group joins and folks adding the game to their Steam wishlist. 

The Rats are equally working hard to make sure that this gets done right. We're getting our Staff prepared to be all-hands-on-deck for Steam's release for a period of 48 hours. On the first day of Steam we suspect the technical team will be busy correcting things that come up suddenly (it always happens in the software development world). On the second day we suspect the dust will settle and it will be all about supporting the users and making sure everything is firing accordingly.

Our primary focus for the first few weeks upon Steam's deployment is to iron out any kinks that may have been unforeseen. That does not however, affect the timeline of development of new content via the Production team. 

All in all, we're ready to get onto Steam mentally (chomping at the bit if you will) but the new server configuration and getting that all firing right, and doing some final testing are some of the last bits remaining. WE ARE ALMOST READY. We'll keep you apprised of our progress as always and ask you to get folks engaged and involved on this matter. Bring back your friends and get them ready, LAUNCH DAY IS COMING SOON. (Seriously)

That's all for now, thanks for reading, and all of us RATS thank you for your support!

Users will launch the game, and before proceeding beyond the persona selection screen they will be prompted to take a non-optional (mandatory) training session of the first 5 basic training tutorials, which include:

[list][*]Movement
[*]Rifle / weapons usage
[*]Chat
[*]Map / using map tools
[*]HUD (Heads up Display)[/list]

Once these tutorials are completed, which will take up to 15 minutes roughly depending on the speed of the user, they will be entered into the regular Campaign and officially start their career in WWII Online. Our team has invested some important time into making sure the tutorials were functioning and there were no road blocks that would cause an issue with users being stuck / unable to proceed. 

We think this is such an important development to ensure the highest levels of success not just for the user but for the game. This will get users into battle faster with more understanding, it is something that really should never be bypassed.

[b]GAME MANAGEMENT PREPARATIONS[/b]

Our new Game Manager "OHM" is preparing for the influx of users and is deep in understanding his new toolset and responsibilities. There will need to be an increase in supply and he'll be at the ready to carefully push numbers upwards as needed. He's also trying to get a new maintenance cycle established, with the hope of making it a bit less frequent and intrusive on Campaign operations. One thing is for sure: the Campaign server must continued to be reset, at a minimum of once per week. With the Campaign coming to new hardware shortly, there may be some changes that are unforeseen, so we'll keep you guys posted as this develops.

OHM is also considering how we can improve the landscape of intermissions and making them a bit more vibrant and interesting. If special events are something you are interested in, you should really connect with him, you can do so by sending him a forum PM.

COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT PREPARATIONS

KMS has been getting his mind blown with all of the stuff required for the Community Manager to do but he's a quick learner and embracing the responsibility. He's also processing a new Assistant Community Manager that will help him with the Axis High Command / Community, filling his recently held position. We'll be announcing who that is in the near future but we think he'll do a great job and the Axis community will be getting an awesome rep.

Keeping the community healthy is paramount for our CM team, so they are strategizing together about expectations and what to prepare for as Steam comes.

[b]HIGH COMMAND OFFICERS - ARE NEEDED (BIG TIME)[/b]

We're going to need an influx of High Command officers to support game operations around the clock for both AHC and GHC. If you can devote a minimum of 3 months service right before Steam's release the Rats would be very grateful. As you know we are deploying on Steam with the brigade system and need as many capable hands in there to help things out and make sure the game stays healthy. Please see the community management team or your HC office for greater details.

[h1]OVERALL PROGRESS - STRONG[/h1]

Thousands of new players are learning about our game everyday, and that's really exciting for us. Steam is continuing to show its power in terms of traffic as it is generating an impressive number of impressions, clicks, Steam group joins and folks adding the game to their Steam wishlist. 

The Rats are equally working hard to make sure that this gets done right. We're getting our Staff prepared to be all-hands-on-deck for Steam's release for a period of 48 hours. On the first day of Steam we suspect the technical team will be busy correcting things that come up suddenly (it always happens in the software development world). On the second day we suspect the dust will settle and it will be all about supporting the users and making sure everything is firing accordingly.

Our primary focus for the first few weeks upon Steam's deployment is to iron out any kinks that may have been unforeseen. That does not however, affect the timeline of development of new content via the Production team. 

All in all, we're ready to get onto Steam mentally (chomping at the bit if you will) but the new server configuration and getting that all firing right, and doing some final testing are some of the last bits remaining. WE ARE ALMOST READY. We'll keep you apprised of our progress as always and ask you to get folks engaged and involved on this matter. Bring back your friends and get them ready, LAUNCH DAY IS COMING SOON. (Seriously)

That's all for now, thanks for reading, and all of us RATS thank you for your support!

notes.title: Update from Rat HQ
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, it's been a while since I've given you an update on what's been going on at Rat HQ. There's been a lot going on behind the scenes!

In the last couple of weeks our Operations team has completed some major work at our CoLo facility in preparation for our launch here on Steam!

We've talked about the install of the upgraded power, but we've also added a new ISP connection that will increase our bandwidth substantially!

These new upgrades have allowed our Operations team, in conjunction with the Development team, to get some new hardware up and running. They have begun configuring this new hardware and it will ultimately help out with our concurrent user capacity and this has been an exciting development internally!

As you can see, all of these much needed upgrades are focused on gearing up for our release here on Steam!

We've still got a lot of work left to go to get all the details ironed out, but our team is dedicated and working hard! We're crossing things off ouf our to-do lists every day!

All of this nuts and bolts detail is a little boring, I know, but it's all very important to the user experience for all of our players, old and new. 

The Production team also has some big things in the works! I heard some awesome things in our internal meeting this week and saw some internal WIP screenshots. Let me just say, I'm excited for when I'll be able to show all of this stuff to you guys. 

We're stil planning on releasing this summer, so thanks for being patient with us and stay tuned for more info!

SALUTE!
